question: How many county magistrates and city mayors will the KMT win in the 2026 Taiwan local elections?

calls.reasoning: KMT has official nominees in only 19 of 22 units (Hsinchu City = independent Kao Hung-an, Chiayi City = TPP-nominated joint candidate, Chiayi County has no KMT nominee), so the 2022 count of 14 is the starting point but Chiayi City cannot be counted. Summing per-race win probabilities from latest polls gives an expected ~11.5: KMT is strong in Taipei, Taoyuan, Taichung, Keelung, Miaoli, Nantou, Yunlin, Taitung, Kinmen and Lienchiang; trails in Changhua (19 vs 36), Yilan and Hsinchu County (both with blue splits); New Taipei and Kaohsiung are near toss-ups; Penghu leans KMT. Pundits project 13-14. Polymarket 'KMT wins most head-of-government races' trades 0.60 vs DPP 0.37 (~$118k volume). That is a near-miss contract, not a seat count, but it suggests a closer race than the pundits. Correlated national swing widens the tails.

- KMT-TPP cooperation is formal, but TPP suspended cooperation in Hsinchu County over a dispute.

- Election date is Nov 28, 2026. Resolves on the count of KMT-officially-nominated winners among the 22 county/city heads; candidates who are only backed by the KMT do not count.
- Event window: now -> Nov 28, 2026 vote; as of 2026-10-18, results not yet known.
- The KMT has nominees in 19 races: Taipei (Chiang Wan-an, incumbent), New Taipei (Lee Shu-chuan), Taoyuan (Chang San-cheng, incumbent), Taichung (Johnny Chiang), Tainan (Hsieh Lung-chieh), Kaohsiung (Ko Chih-en), Keelung (Hsieh Kuo-liang, incumbent), Yilan (Wu Tsung-hsien, joint KMT-TPP), Hsinchu County (Hsu Hsin-ying), Miaoli (Chung Tung-chin, incumbent), Changhua (Wei Ping-cheng), Nantou (Hsu Shu-hua, incumbent), Yunlin (Chang Chia-chun), Pingtung (Su Ching-chuan), Hualien, Taitung, Penghu (Chen Chen-chung), Kinmen (Chen Yu-chen vs 6 independents), Lienchiang. No KMT nominee in Chiayi City (TPP Chang Chi-kai), Chiayi County or Hsinchu City (independent incumbent Ann Kao). (Wikipedia, Sep-Oct 2026)
- Past KMT wins: 14 in 2022 (including Chiayi City and Yilan), 15 in 2018, 6 in 2014.
- Taipei: TVBS Oct 8-10 poll has Chiang 49%, DPP's Puma Shen 41%; the gap was 28 pts in late May. TVBS Oct 17: 41% expect Shen to do better in the debate vs 30% for Chiang. Debate is Oct 31.
- New Taipei: Hsin-min Association poll (released Oct 13) has DPP's Su Chiao-hui 43.1% vs Lee 30%. A KMT city-council caucus poll has Lee 42.6% vs Su 35.9%.
- Taichung: polls show Chiang ahead of DPP's Ho Hsin-chun by 1.9 (pro-green group, Oct 5-6), 6.0 (Era, Oct 7) and 11.1 (KMT caucus, Oct 15-16).
- Changhua (open seat): ETtoday Aug 2026 has DPP's Chen Su-yueh 36.4% vs Wei 19.4%, 28% undecided; DPP defector Chiu Chien-fu is running as an independent. KMT chair says its own polling is favorable (Oct 17).
- Yilan: Formosa poll had Wu 33.0% vs DPP's Lin Kuo-chang 35.8%; TVBS had Lin +3; Lin's internal poll has him +9.8.
- Hsinchu County: Daai poll (Sep 21) has DPP's Cheng Chao-fang 35.1% vs Hsu 28.7%; an April poll had Hsu +11. A blue-white rift is reported.
- Keelung: KMT party poll (Oct) has Hsieh 42.9% vs DPP's Tung Tzu-wei 38.3%; DPP claims its internal poll shows it leading.
- Penghu: Chen Chen-chung 30.3% leads DPP's Wu Shu-chin by 9.3. Kinmen: Chen Yu-chen 45.4% vs 10.7% for the runner-up (KMT-side poll, Sep).

calls.reference_class: KMT county/city head wins in Taiwan local elections 2014-2022 (6, 15, 14), adjusted to current nominations

calls.reasoning: KMT has official nominees in only 19 of 22 races, so Chiayi City, counted in its 2022 total of 14, is excluded. Summing per-race win probabilities from October polls gives an expected ~11.4 seats. Strong: Taipei, Taoyuan, Taichung, Miaoli, Nantou, Lienchiang, Kinmen, Taitung, Yunlin, Hualien. Lean KMT: Keelung. Toss-ups: New Taipei, Penghu. Lean DPP: Hsinchu County, Yilan, Kaohsiung. Unlikely: Changhua, Pingtung, Tainan. October polls show a DPP current, so the self-interested KMT target and older pundit projections of 13-14 are discounted. Polymarket's plurality contract (KMT 0.60, DPP 0.37) is a near-miss used as evidence, not an anchor, and is consistent with ~11 KMT seats. Correlated swing widens the tails.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the key facts: 19 KMT nominees, none in Hsinchu City, Chiayi City or Chiayi County; the same polls; and the same history. Factual disputes: (1) Yilan joint KMT-TPP label vs KMT nominee: compatible, since Wu is the official KMT nominee, so his race counts. (2) Keelung poll sponsor, Trend vs KMT party: unresolved without web access, so Keelung is treated as only leaning KMT (0.6). (3) Penghu polls conflict: unresolved, so treated as a toss-up. Judgment: I weight October polls over the KMT's self-estimate of 13-14. My own per-race sum is ~11.4, slightly above Runs 2 and 3, because Kaohsiung (one poll tied) and Penghu get non-trivial probability. I carry forward roughly the runs' dispersion.
